dialogReference.para: Area to cover. Leave blank for the current map view.
DTM: the bare-ground surface, predicted by machine learning; use it for fault mapping. DSM: the top of trees and buildings (five bands, about five times the data to stream).
Which DSM band: dsm (the surface), its 5th, 50th or 95th percentile, or dsm_std (the spread of heights within each pixel).
The GeoTIFF to write (in a folder, not a geodatabase).
Leave blank to keep the tiles' native UTM grid (one zone) or pick one automatically. Choose a projected system in metres, never degrees.

Also write these as GeoTIFFs beside the clip: Hillshade (lit from the chosen sun), slope in degrees (added switched off) and local relief model (LRM: height above or below the local mean, blue to red over +/- 2.5 m).

Each pixel's height minus the mean height within this distance. Smaller radii show narrow features: 150 m for offset channels and narrow scarps, 300 m for scarps tens of metres wide, 1000 m for broad scarps and fold scarps (slow when live).
Height of the sun above the horizon, in degrees. A low sun brings out low scarps: about 20 on plains, 30-35 in steep country.
The tool stops before reading anything if the estimated download is larger. 0 means no limit.

Multidirectional lights the surface from several directions, so no scarp orientation is hidden. A single sun, or one shining across a fault trend, gives scarps facing it up to three times the contrast.
Direction the sun shines from, in degrees clockwise from north (for a single sun). 315 (north-west) is usual.

Trend of the fault you are mapping, in degrees (either direction along it, e.g. 30 for a NNE-SSW fault). The sun is put at right angles to it, on the side nearer north-west, so relief does not look inverted.
Vertical exaggeration of the hillshade. 1 shows true relief; 2-3 brings out subtle scarps on Australian plains, along with the DTM's noise.

summary.para: Download the GEM-15 pixels for an extent into a local GeoTIFF, after estimating the download, with optional hillshade, slope and local relief model GeoTIFFs.

usage.bullet_item: Tiles in one UTM zone keep their native 15 m grid; across zones they are resampled (bilinear), which smooths scarp faces: measure on a single-zone clip where you can.
The DTM costs roughly 150 MB per 1-degree cell at Australian latitudes; the DSM about five times that. Cancel stops the download.
Draw the extent a little larger than you need: near its edge the LRM uses part of its circle.
